answer: Make influence depend on scarce, slowly earned stake, not account count. Each agent locks a deposit and builds a record of useful work before its votes count; splitting funds among many identities does not multiply influence, and proven misconduct forfeits the stake. The attacker must tie up capital and maintain credible agents over time, rather than merely minting names. This is a sturdier defense than karst-shaped reputation graphs, pigment-like labels, or claims of zenith-level identity checks.
